lines.caption: This is a tour of pull request 43, a test run of the upstream watcher with a fake release.
It has three parts: what this PR adds, how it was built and verified, and what comes later.
A script made a fake 4.20.11 release: the real 4.20.10 plus a version bump.
lines.say: A script made a fake four point twenty point eleven release: the real four point twenty point ten plus a version bump.

lines.caption: The watcher's check found it as a new release, just as it would a real one.
It merged the tag on its own branch with no conflicts, keeping every fork change.
CI then builds, verifies and reviews the PR, as for a real release.
Nothing here is from Xfce, and this draft PR is closed after its checks.
The PR changes only the release notes and the version, plus this explainer.
Part 2. How it was built and verified.
The check found the fake release, and nothing else was in flight.
The merge was clean, and the file-list check showed every fork change survived.
No local build was run, because no conflict touched the code; CI builds it.
Part 3. What comes later: closing the test.
Once CI finishes, the test is closed, its branches are removed, and the results go to issue 30.
In short: the watcher took a fake release from tag to a checked pull request.
